lines.trans: Funny—I walked past these grey shutters every morning and stopped seeing them!
Because the climbing ivy grew right across the middle iron hook!
Don't cut the vine, Nour; lift the green branch gently onto the trellis.
Look! All the leaves stay safe, and now we can reach the iron latch!
Let me pull—ugh! It will not budge a single millimetre!
Oil first, muscle second, boss. Two drops on each hinge pin.
Give the oil ten seconds... now lift slightly and pull together!
One, two—there goes the left shutter!
And the right one! Look how big the courtyard looks with glass on two sides!
Wave through the clean window—Suad is smiling at the piano inside!
We definitely need fresh green paint on this dry grey wood tomorrow.
Sandpaper tonight, green paint Monday morning—if the sky stays dry.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: خضرا, plural: خضر).

examples.trans: Pass beside the green pharmacy.
Put the green herbs on the eggs.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بأشر, بيأشر).

examples.trans: Salma motioned to me from the kitchen.
Rami is pointing to the two chairs.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بعطي, بيعطي).

examples.trans: Did the shopkeeper give you a receipt?
Give me the breakfast bag, please.

meanings.note: Means 'certainly, definitely' or 'must be' (إنتي أكيد نور 'you must be Nour').

examples.trans: Hello! You must be Nour.

examples.text: أكيد صاحبه رح يدور عليه قريبا.
examples.trans: Surely its owner will look for it soon.

meanings.note: A sigh of dismay or tiredness, a little like English 'oof' or 'ugh'.

examples.trans: Oof, I forgot the key at home!
Ugh, it's hot today.

meanings.note: Before an indefinite noun أول means 'first' (أول يوم 'first day'); after a definite noun الأول / الأولى agrees in gender (الصفحة الأولى 'the first page'). Also used adverbially ('first').

examples.trans: Welcome on your first day of work!
Read the first page calmly.

meanings.note: Everyday conditional word 'if' for real possibilities.

examples.text: رني الجرس إذا احتجتي أي شي.
examples.trans: Ring the bell if you need anything.

examples.text: إذا فتحنا الساحة الصبح، الجيران بيفرحوا.
examples.trans: If we open the courtyard in the morning, the neighbours will be delighted.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (ببتسم, بيبتسم).

examples.trans: Smile when the bell rings!
He smiled when he saw his brother.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian form of الاثنين ('Monday', and with ال also 'both / the two').

examples.trans: I started work on Monday morning.
Monday's bus arrived at seven.

meanings.note: Signature Levantine word for 'want / need', inflected with pronoun suffixes: بدي (I want), بدك (you want), بده (he/it wants), بدها (she/it wants), بدنا (we want), بدكم (you pl. want), بدهم (they want).

examples.trans: I want to read the booking ledger.
Jam bread needs unsalted butter.

بطّل.gloss: to stop (doing); no longer be able

meanings.en: to stop (doing); no longer be able
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (ببطل, بيبطل).

examples.trans: My knees stopped holding me up from the shock!
The rain stopped falling in the morning.

meanings.note: Everyday word for 'tomorrow' (بكرا الصبح 'tomorrow morning').

examples.text: بكرا الصبح رح نسبق المي الباردة!
examples.trans: Tomorrow morning we will beat the cold water!
We booked a quiet dinner — will you join us tomorrow?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: بيانوهات.

examples.trans: The sound of the piano is warm and calm.
I learned piano when I was young.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: تانية, plural: تانيين).

examples.trans: Room four is on the second floor.
There is a second sheet behind the letter.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بتحرك, بيتحرك).

examples.text: في قطعة معدن تحركت جوا الصندوق!
examples.trans: A piece of metal shifted inside the box!
The car pulled away from the door.

meanings.note: Wooden or iron garden trellis supporting climbing jasmine, grapevines, or ivy.

examples.text: رفعنا عرق اللبلاب شوي شوي عالتعريشة.
examples.trans: We lifted the ivy vine gently onto the trellis.

examples.text: القعدة تحت تعريشة الياسمين بالصيف بترد الروح.
examples.trans: Sitting under the jasmine trellis in summer refreshes the soul.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'two' (إنتو التنين 'the two of you'); note homograph التنين ('Monday').

examples.trans: He has two left on the shelf.
Hold the torch, the two of you!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: ثواني.

examples.trans: Wait one second, please.
He came back ten seconds later on the dot.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: جديدة, plural: جداد).

examples.trans: I am Nour, the new receptionist.
I installed a new lightbulb last week.

meanings.note: Used with right and left: الجهة اليمين 'the right side', من هاي الجهة 'from this side'.

examples.trans: The kitchen is on the other side.
Walk this way, it is closer.

meanings.note: Used both before a noun ('inside the bag') and standalone ('inside').

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
The water is flowing inside!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: The iron gate is locked at night.
Pass me the heavy iron wrench.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أخشاب.

examples.trans: The wooden ceiling is warm and quiet.
This is a hand-carved wooden train.

meanings.note: Very frequent Jordanian verb: خليني ('let me'), خلينا ('let us'), خليك ('stay!'), خلي ('keep/leave').

examples.trans: Let us open the door together.
Hot bread makes people pleasant!

meanings.note: Small metal pin, tack, or brass hinge pivot pin.

examples.text: دبوس المفصلة النحاس صغير كتير وبده ملقط.
examples.trans: The brass hinge pin is tiny and requires tweezers.

examples.text: علقت الورقة على اللوح بدبوس صغير.
examples.trans: I pinned the note onto the board with a small tack.

meanings.note: Single hinged panel or leaf of a double window, shutter, or cupboard.

examples.text: فتحنا الدرفة الشمال وبعدين الدرفة اليمين.
examples.trans: We swung open the left shutter leaf and then the right one.

examples.text: كل شباك إله درفتين خشب متينات.
examples.trans: Each window has two sturdy wooden shutter panels.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: دهانات.

examples.trans: Room eight has fresh paint.

examples.text: ريحة الدهان راحت لما فتحنا الشباك.
examples.trans: The smell of paint cleared when we opened the window.

meanings.note: With مش (مش راضي يفتح), idiomatically means a stubborn door or latch 'refuses to / won't' budge!

examples.text: القفل القديم مش راضي يتحرك بدون نقطة زيت.
examples.trans: The old lock refuses to budge without a drop of oil.

examples.text: الكل طلع راضي ومبسوط من طعم الشوربة.
examples.trans: Everyone came away happy and satisfied with the soup.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (برفع, بيرفع).

examples.trans: Lift the handle first and then push.
He raised his cup in a toast to the neighbours.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: رمادية, plural: رماديين).

examples.trans: He is wearing a dark grey coat.

examples.text: بدنا نحمي بيتنا من المكاتب الرمادية.
examples.trans: We want to protect our house from grey offices.

meanings.note: Used almost universally in the Levantine adverbial phrase بالزبط (biz-zabt, 'exactly / right on').

examples.text: هاد هو اللون الأخضر اللي بدنا إياه بالزبط!
examples.trans: That is the exact shade of green we want!

examples.text: وصل السايق عالباب الساعة تنتين بالزبط.
examples.trans: The driver arrived at the gate at two o'clock sharp.

meanings.note: Cooking oil (زيت زيتون 'olive oil') or machine/hinge oil.

examples.text: حطينا نقطتين زيت على كل مفصلة حديد.
examples.trans: We put two drops of oil on every iron hinge.

examples.text: شوربة العدس بتطلع أطيب مع رشة زيت زيتون.
examples.trans: Lentil soup tastes even better with a drizzle of olive oil.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: ساحات.

examples.trans: The courtyard has a big jasmine tree.
We sat drinking tea in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Pull a door, a drawer or a heavy thing; also to withdraw money from a bank.

examples.trans: Pull the door towards you, don't push it.
I took money out of the bank this morning.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: سليمة, plural: سليمين).

examples.trans: Thank goodness your cup is still intact!
All the plates arrived unbroken.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: سماوات.

examples.trans: The evening sky is clear and calm.
The lanterns are glowing beneath the sky.

meanings.note: Everyday Levantine word for 'together'.

examples.trans: Let us open the door together.
We drank morning coffee together in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to see, look, check' (بشوف / شاف).

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
I will see you tomorrow at breakfast.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: شبابيك.

examples.trans: The window overlooks the courtyard tree.
We painted the wooden shutters in summer.

meanings.note: In everyday Jordanian directions, شمال (shmaal) means 'left' (contrast شَمال shamaal 'north').

examples.trans: Turn left at the street corner.
The key is on the shelf to your left.

meanings.note: Traditional Levantine word for an iron hook-and-eye latch on wooden shutters or doors.

examples.text: رفعنا شنكل الحديد ففتح الشيش فورا.
examples.trans: We lifted the iron hook latch and the shutter swung right open.

examples.text: سكر شنكل الشباك منيح قبل ما تنام.
examples.trans: Fasten the window latch securely before going to sleep.

شوي.gloss: a little; a moment (شوي شوي slowly)

meanings.en: a little; a moment (شوي شوي slowly)
meanings.note: Means 'a bit / a moment' (استنوا شوي 'wait a moment'); doubled شوي شوي means 'slowly, gently'.

examples.trans: Wait a moment, I have an idea!
Turn the valve slowly and gently.

meanings.note: Levantine word for slatted window shutters, used as a collective: الشيش مسكر 'the shutters are closed'.

examples.trans: Close the shutters, the sun is strong.
Green shutters suit the house.

meanings.note: Describes a pure musical note, clear sky (سما صافية), or clear broth.

examples.text: نغمة البيانو طلعت صافية متل المي.
examples.trans: The piano note rang out crystal clear.

examples.text: انشالله تضل السما صافية طول نهار التنين.
examples.trans: Hopefully the sky stays clear all day Monday.

meanings.note: Everyday spoken Jordanian noun for 'the morning' (الصبح in the morning, كل صبح every morning).

examples.trans: I drink black coffee every morning.
The morning bread is still hot.

meanings.note: Woodworker's word for sanding timber smooth; ورق صنفرة is sandpaper.

examples.text: خلصنا صنفرة الدرفات الأربعة قبل المغرب.
examples.trans: We finished sanding all four shutter panels before sunset.

examples.text: اشتريت ورق صنفرة ناعم للخشب القديم.
examples.trans: I bought fine-grit sandpaper for the old wood.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بضل, بيضل).

examples.trans: Family is what remains.
My teacup stayed intact inside the suitcase!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian hollow verb (بطال / بنطال) meaning 'reach a high shelf or latch'.

examples.text: ما بقدر أطال الرف الفوقاني بدون سلم.
examples.trans: I can't reach the top shelf without a ladder.

examples.text: بعدنا الغصن وهلا بنطال الشنكل بسهولة.
examples.trans: We moved the branch aside and now we can reach the hook easily.

meanings.note: Slender climbing stem or root of jasmine, mint, or ivy ('iriq, pl. 'ruuq).

examples.text: حطيت عرق نعنع أخضر بكاسة الشاي السخن.
examples.trans: I put a sprig of fresh green mint into the glass of hot tea.

examples.text: عرق اللبلاب طلع عالحيط الحجر لحد الشباك.
examples.trans: The ivy vine climbed up the stone wall right to the window.

meanings.note: Numeral 'ten'; short form عشر ('ashar) before a plural noun (عشر دقايق 'ten minutes').

examples.trans: You arrived ten minutes early.
Breakfast is from seven-thirty to ten.

meanings.note: Used literally or humorously (الزيت أول والعضلات تاني 'oil first, muscle second').

examples.text: فتح الشباك القديم بده نقطة زيت مش عضلات!
examples.trans: Opening the old window takes a drop of oil, not brute muscle!

examples.text: تعبوا عضلات إيدي من حمل السطول عالدرج.
examples.trans: My arm muscles got tired from carrying buckets up the stairs.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition 'on, at, to'; before ال- it regularly contracts to عال- ('al- / 'a-).

examples.trans: Your glasses are on your forehead!
Say hello to Salma for me!

meanings.note: Levantine progressive marker placed before a present-tense verb to show action happening right now.

examples.trans: The water is flowing inside the pipe right now!

examples.text: كنت عم بدور على دفتري هلا.
examples.trans: I was just looking for my notebook.

meanings.note: Marks location ('at, by') and with pronoun suffixes expresses possession: عندي ('I have'), عندك ('you have'), عندنا ('we have').

examples.trans: A taxi just stopped at the door.
I have a reservation under the name Suad.

meanings.note: As an adjective غريب / غريبة means 'strange, odd'; as a noun (plural غرباء) it means 'stranger(s)'.

examples.trans: I heard a strange metallic knock at night.
Why would he leave his bag with strangers?

meanings.note: Leafy branch of a tree or climbing shrub.

examples.text: رفعنا الغصن الأخضر عن شنكل الشباك بلطف.
examples.trans: We gently lifted the green branch off the window latch.

examples.text: عصفور صغير وقف على غصن شجرة الليمون.
examples.trans: A little bird perched on a branch of the lemon tree.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بفتح, بيفتح).

examples.trans: The corner shop opens at seven.
Oh, the door finally opened!

meanings.note: Used both before a noun ('above, over') and standalone ('upstairs').

examples.trans: The window is above the old tree.
Let us go upstairs to see the room.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for 'in front of, before'.

examples.trans: The golden lanterns against the evening sky.
The car is parked in front of the gate.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بقدر, بيقدر).

examples.text: بنقدر نقدم زبدة مالحة مع المربى؟
examples.trans: Can we serve salted butter with jam?

examples.text: ليش ما قدرت تعطيه القطار بإيدك؟
examples.trans: Why could you not hand him the train yourself?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: قريبة, plural: قراب).

examples.text: علمت بيانو ببيت قريب من هون.
examples.trans: I taught piano in a house near here.
We booked a table at a nearby restaurant.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian form of زجاج ('glass').

examples.trans: Look at the courtyard through the window glass.
We wiped the glass this morning until it shone.

قص.gloss: to cut; snip; trim (with scissors or shears)

meanings.en: to cut; snip; trim (with scissors or shears)
meanings.note: Geminate verb for cutting stems, paper, or tape cleanly.

examples.text: لا تقص عرق الياسمين الأخضر، ارفعه لفوق.
examples.trans: Don't cut the green jasmine stem—lift it upward.
I cut a strip of black tape for the wire.

meanings.note: Arabic uses no 'is/are' in the simple present, while كان supplies the past ('was/were') and يكون / بيكون supplies future or modal 'be'.

examples.trans: How was the bus ride?

examples.text: تاني يوم ما رح يكون ممل!
examples.trans: The second day will not be boring!

meanings.note: Intransitive verb (past كبرت kbirt 'I grew up') from the root ك-ب-ر ('big, great').

examples.text: زياد ورامي كبروا قريب من سوق السبت.
examples.trans: Ziad and Rami grew up near the Saturday market.

examples.text: شجرة الياسمين كبرت ووصلت للطابق التاني.
examples.trans: The jasmine tree grew and reached the second floor.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: كبيرة, plural: كبار).

examples.trans: We use this big paper ledger.
You know older brothers well!

meanings.note: Before an indefinite singular noun كل means 'every' (كل يوم 'every day'); before a definite noun it means 'all / the whole' (كل الأسبوع 'all week').

examples.trans: Tell me everything I need to know.
Everyone is happy in the courtyard today.

كمان.gloss: also; too; again (كمان مرة once more)

meanings.en: also; too; again (كمان مرة once more)
meanings.note: Everyday Levantine word for 'also, too, more' (كمان مرة 'one more time / again').

examples.text: التفكير السريع أنقذ الفطور كمان مرة!
examples.trans: Quick thinking saved breakfast once again!
And I missed you too.

meanings.note: Takes pronoun suffixes in spoken Jordanian: لأني (because I), لأنك (because you), لأنه (because he/it — also general 'because'), لأنكم (because you pl.).

examples.text: لأنه القهوة الطيبة بتخلي الناس لطاف!
examples.trans: Because good coffee makes people pleasant!
Thank you because you kept the bag safe.

meanings.note: Standalone لا means 'no'; before a 2nd-person subjunctive verb it forms a negative command (لا تقلقي 'do not worry!'), and لا ... ولا means 'neither ... nor'.

examples.trans: No, lift the handle first.
Do not worry, ma'am.

meanings.note: Climbing green ivy covering courtyard stone walls.

examples.text: اللبلاب الأخضر غطى نص حيط الساحة القديم.
examples.trans: Green ivy covered half of the old courtyard wall.

examples.text: ورق اللبلاب بيلمع تحت المي بعد المطر.
examples.trans: The ivy leaves glisten after the rain.

meanings.note: Definite الليلة means 'tonight', while indefinite ليلة means 'one night / night of'.

examples.trans: I am going to sleep well tonight.
We booked the room for three nights.

meanings.note: Negates verbs and في (ما بعرف 'I don't know', ما في 'there isn't'), and links conjunctions like قبل ما ('before') and بعد ما ('after').

examples.trans: Paper does not lose room names.
Have tea before you head out.

meanings.note: Polite everyday Jordanian address for an adult woman or female guest.

examples.trans: Good morning, madam, please come in!
The room is booked under Madam Suad.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بمر, بيمر).

examples.trans: Pass right beside the green pharmacy.

examples.text: أنا مريت من جنب السبيل الحجري!
examples.trans: I just passed the stone fountain!

meanings.note: Negates nouns, adjectives, participles, and pronouns in spoken Jordanian (مش شنتتي 'not my bag', مش ملاقي 'cannot find').

examples.trans: This is not my suitcase!
Not bad for a second day at work!

meanings.note: Everyday preposition 'with'; takes pronoun suffixes to express 'have on one's person' (معي 'I have with me', معك حق 'you are right').

examples.trans: You are right, Nour!
Goodbye! (lit. go with safety)

meanings.note: Describes climbing vines like ivy, jasmine, or grapevines.

examples.text: الياسمين المعرش عالقوس بلش يفتح ورد أبيض.
examples.trans: The climbing jasmine on the archway has started opening white blossoms.

examples.text: اللبلاب المعرش غطى الشنكل الحديد كله.
examples.trans: The climbing ivy covered the iron hook completely.

meanings.note: In Jordanian speech, يا معلم is an affectionate, respectful way to address a boss or skilled craftsperson.

examples.trans: You are all generosity, boss!
She was a very gifted piano teacher.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: مفصلات.

examples.text: حطيت نقطة زيت على مفصلة الباب.
examples.trans: I put a drop of oil on the door hinge.
The brass hinges of the chest are intact.

meanings.note: Everyday short form of مليمتر ('millimetre'); ولا ملي ('not a single millimetre').

examples.text: الشنكل المصدي ما تحرك ولا ملي قبل الزيت.
examples.trans: The rusty latch wouldn't budge a single millimetre before the oil.

examples.text: قاس رامي عرض البرواز بالمتر والملي.
examples.trans: Rami measured the width of the frame down to the millimetre.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition meaning 'from', 'of', or 'than' after comparatives.

examples.trans: I am Salma from the kitchen.
Breakfast is from seven-thirty to ten.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: ناشفة, plural: ناشفين).

examples.trans: Here is a dry towel for your coat.
The attic is dry and warm in the rain.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: نظيفة, plural: نظاف).

examples.trans: The desk is clean and the room is ready.

examples.text: آسف نقطت مي على أرضكم النظيفة.
examples.trans: Sorry I dripped water onto your clean floor.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: نقط.

examples.trans: Not a single drop of juice got on the table!

examples.text: شرب كل نقطة من الشوربة السخنة.
examples.trans: He drank every drop of the hot soup.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian demonstrative ('this / that'); feminine هادي (haadi), plural هدول (hadool). Before ال- it also contracts to هال-.

examples.trans: Here we use this big ledger.
This suitcase is very heavy today.

meanings.note: Signature Levantine word for 'now / right now' (pronounced halla' in Amman).

examples.trans: A taxi just stopped at the door now.
We will check the tag right now.

meanings.note: Used both as the numeral 'one' and after a noun for emphasis ('a single, one and the same').

examples.trans: Not a single scratch on the cup!
The gate rang with one strong ring.

meanings.note: Collective ورق ('paper / tree leaves'), singulative ورقة ('a sheet of paper / note'), plural أوراق ('documents / papers').

examples.trans: We use a paper ledger and a pencil.
He wrote a note on a small slip of paper.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian adjective from وسط ('middle'); pairs naturally with المفتاح الوسطاني and ري الوسطى.

examples.text: المفتاح الوسطاني بالبيانو كان عالق من الرطوبة.
examples.trans: The middle key on the piano was stuck from dampness.

examples.text: الطاولة الوسطانية بالساحة بتاخد أحلى شمس.
examples.trans: The middle table in the courtyard catches the nicest sunshine.

meanings.note: With two pronunciations in context: walla ('or' in choice questions: عالشارع ولا عالساحة؟) and wala ('not even / nor': ولا خدش 'not a single scratch', ولا يهمك 'do not worry at all').

examples.trans: Is the window facing the street or the courtyard?
Not a single drop of water on the table!

meanings.note: Placed directly before a name or title when addressing someone in Arabic (يا نور 'Nour!', يا أستاذ 'sir!') and in exclamations (يا سلام! 'wonderful!').

examples.trans: Good morning, Tariq!
Oh, how lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: The green pharmacy is on your right.
We hung the board to the right of the desk.
